# Removing affine obstructions from double-divergence tests without a global lower bound

[Family 091](../families/openai-math-091.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000086.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $\mu$ have a smooth, strictly positive, even probability density on $\mathbb R^n$. Let $\tau$ be smooth, even and symmetric, with $0<\tau(x)\le\Lambda I$. Put $Af=x\cdot\nabla f-\tau:D^2f$. Assume both

$$\mathbb E[hAf]=\mathbb E[\nabla h\cdot\tau\nabla f],\qquad
\mathbb E[(Af)(A-1)f]=\mathbb E\|\tau^{1/2}D^2f\,\tau^{1/2}\|_F^2$$

for compact smooth tests. Then the $L^2(\mu)$ closure of $\{A(A-1)f:f\in C_c^\infty,\ f\text{ even}\}$ is the entire centered even subspace.

The proof first shows that every $L^2$ distributional solution of $A(A-1)g=0$ is affine. Local ellipticity gives smoothness. Cutoff estimates establish $Ag\in L^2$ before splitting $g=(g-Ag)+Ag$ into eigenvalue-zero and eigenvalue-one parts. The first is constant; graph-norm cutoff approximation and the Hessian identity force the second to be linear. Parity and centering then remove both obstructions.

## Role in the source argument

Extends a dual variance inequality from compactly supported double divergences to arbitrary centered even L2 tests. This justifies substituting the unbounded polynomial slab observable into the final dual inequality.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:density](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/density.tex#L7)
- [eq:density-two-estimates](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/density.tex#L85)
- [eq:hessian](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-logarithmic-Brunn-Minkowski-conjecture-September-23-2026/build/identities.tex#L106)

## Antecedents and comparison

The operator belongs to the moment-measure diffusion of [Klartag](https://arxiv.org/abs/1309.2767v1); the source credits the transport-Hessian identity to [Kolesnikov–Livshyts–Rotem](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.12099v3). Orthogonal-complement density and cutoff methods are standard. The useful formulation here requires only local strict positivity and a global upper matrix bound, with the necessary operator identities stated explicitly.

## Checks and limitations

Read the cutoff estimates, the L2 splitting and the graph-norm approximation in full. The bundled calculation checks the Gaussian Hermite model, where A has eigenvalues k and A(A-1) has eigenvalues k(k-1).

The Gaussian check illustrates the affine kernel; it does not establish density for a general matrix field. Neither parity nor the Hessian identity can be silently omitted. No operator-domain assertion is assumed merely from the formal expression for A.

## Possible applications

A reusable density argument when a weighted second-order operator has an affine kernel, its coefficients may degenerate at infinity, and a compact-test Hessian identity is available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Weighted relative moments can be separated into simultaneous embedding coordinates

[Family 094](../families/openai-math-094.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000087.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For distinct $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ in a real $L_p$ space, $1<p<\infty$, write $E$ for the pairs, $\delta_{ij}=\|x_i-x_j\|_p$ and

$$V=\{((z_i-z_j)/\delta_{ij})_{ij\in E}:z\in\mathbb R^n\}.$$

Fix $0<\eta<1/3$ and $b,K\ge1$. Suppose that for **every** strictly positive probability vector $\lambda$ on $E$, a random $F\in V$ exists with $\|F\|_\infty\le K$ almost surely and

$$\sum_e\lambda_e\left|\mathbb E|F_e|^p-b\right|\le\eta b.$$

The distribution may depend on $\lambda$, but $b$ and $K$ must not. Then one obtains an embedding into $\ell_p^d$ with distortion at most $((1+3\eta)/(1-3\eta))^{1/p}$ and

$$d\le\left\lceil C\max\{1,K^{2p}/(\eta^2b^2)\}\log(2n)\right\rceil,$$

where $C$ is absolute. Separate the compact convex set of possible moment vectors from the open coordinate box of radius $2\eta b$. A separating functional $a$, normalized in ell_1, is tested with $\lambda_e=3|a_e|/4+1/(4|E|)$, giving the incompatible bounds $2\eta b$ and $4\eta b/3$. One common distribution therefore exists; bounded independent sampling and a union bound add at most another $\eta b$ per coordinate.

## Role in the source argument

Separates the construction of scalar random increments from the simultaneous embedding requirement. Allowing a common moment b larger than one makes an additive moment error small relative to the metric scale.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:weighted](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L295)
- [eq:sampling-dimension](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L309)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Eskenazis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.06602) uses Maurey’s empirical method, distance matrices and a change of measure to obtain additive-error dimension reduction for incompressible sets. The source seeks uniform relative control for arbitrary configurations through a weighted test criterion. Convex separation and the concentration step themselves are standard.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the separating-functional argument, positivity of its test weights, the sampling tail exponent and the conversion from pth moments to a common distance scale.

An existential distribution for each pair separately is insufficient. Bounds that depend on the testing probability do not satisfy the hypothesis. This criterion alone provides neither the required distributions nor an efficient algorithm.

## Possible applications

A modular way to assemble metric embeddings from weighted scalar tests, or to identify exactly where a randomized-coordinate construction lacks uniform relative error.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# A fixed-point reweighting turns average electrical localization into uniform row control

[Family 094](../families/openai-math-094.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000087.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Use the normalized-gradient space $V$ above. For each positive pair probability $\lambda$, there is a probability $\sigma\ge\lambda/2$ such that the orthogonal projection $P$ onto $V$ in $\ell_2(\sigma)$ satisfies

$$\|P\|_{\infty\to\infty}=\max_e\sum_f|P_{ef}|\le4\log(2n).$$

Both $P$ and $I-P$ remain contractions in $\ell_2(\sigma)$. To obtain the weights, let $R_e(\sigma)=\sum_f|P_{ef}(\sigma)|$ and $L=2\log n$. The established electrical localization bound implies $\sum_e\sigma_eR_e^2\le L^2$. On $\{\sigma:\sum\sigma=1,\ \sigma\ge\lambda/2\}$ define

$$u_e(\sigma)=\frac{\sigma_eR_e(\sigma)^2}{2L^2},\qquad
\Phi_e(\sigma)=u_e(\sigma)+(1-\sum_fu_f(\sigma))\lambda_e.$$

This is a continuous self-map because $\sum u\le1/2$. At a Brouwer fixed point, $u_e\le\sigma_e$ gives $R_e\le\sqrt2L$, which is the stated bound. The positive lower weights keep the projection’s Gram matrix invertible on the compact domain.

## Role in the source argument

Projects clipped or truncated random increments back onto increments arising from consistent point labels, controlling both the L2 error and the coordinate magnitude.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:localization](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L392)
- [lem:projection](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L410)
- [eq:average-row-sums](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L433)

## Antecedents and comparison

The logarithmic bound for the entrywise absolute transfer-current matrix is the theorem of [Gurel-Gurevich, Nachmias and Sachdeva](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24130v1). This card extracts the subsequent weight selection, not that established localization theorem as a new discovery. Brouwer reweighting is an established general technique; priority for this particular projection formulation is unresolved.

## Checks and limitations

The proof of the self-map and its row estimate was checked. Finite complete-graph examples verify the conjugation to a Euclidean projection, the weighted average row identity and the fixed-point inequalities at numerical solutions.

Numerical fixed-point iteration is only a check on examples: Brouwer’s theorem does not imply convergence of the naive iteration. The bound concerns this graph-gradient projection and does not hold automatically for arbitrary subspaces.

## Possible applications

A template for turning an averaged matrix bound into simultaneous row bounds while preserving a prescribed fraction of every original test weight.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Antipodal row and column incidences force quadratic exact coordinate dimension

[Family 094](../families/openai-math-094.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000087.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix $1<p<\infty$, $p\ne2$, and integer $k\ge2$. In $\ell_p^{k^2}$ let $r_i$ and $c_j$ be the indicator vectors of the rows and columns of a $k\times k$ grid. The $4k+1$ points

$$\{0\}\cup\{r_i,-r_i:1\le i\le k\}\cup\{c_j,-c_j:1\le j\le k\}$$

require at least $k^2$ coordinates in any isometric ell_p embedding, even an unrestricted nonlinear one. Translate and rescale a distortion-one map to fix zero. Strict convexity forces preservation of antipodes. The p-parallelogram defect

$$\|u+v\|_p^p+\|u-v\|_p^p-2\|u\|_p^p-2\|v\|_p^p$$

vanishes exactly when the supports are disjoint: every nonzero scalar defect has the sign of $p-2$. The images of different rows therefore have disjoint supports, as do different columns. Every row–column pair has defect $2^p-4\ne0$, so their image supports intersect. A coordinate can witness at most one of the $k^2$ incidences. For arbitrary $n\ge9$, padding gives the lower bound $\lfloor(n-1)/4\rfloor^2$.

## Role in the source argument

Explains the discontinuity between exact coordinate realization and the source’s approximate dimension reduction, including even integer exponents greater than two.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:disjointness](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L1079)
- [eq:antipodes](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L1099)
- [eq:exact-bounds](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/Subpolynomial-dimension-reduction-in-Lp-September-23-2026/build/paper.tex#L92)

## Antecedents and comparison

The support test is classical: [Lamperti, Corollary 2.1](https://msp.org/pjm/1958/8-3/pjm-v8-n3-p09-s.pdf). The source credits Ball’s earlier quadratic-order sharpness for 1<=p<2. The candidate extracted device is the finite antipodal incidence configuration extending this argument across p>2; no claim of exhaustive novelty verification is made.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the scalar-sign proof and strict-convexity step. The bundled finite calculation verifies all row/column defects and support incidences for several grid sizes, with p=2 as a negative control.

Exact equality is essential; the proof gives no comparable dimension lower bound at fixed distortion greater than one. Strict convexity excludes p=1 from this argument, and the defect vanishes identically at p=2.

## Possible applications

Encoding combinatorial incidence constraints into exact metric realizations, and constructing small certificates that a proposed coordinate compression cannot preserve all distances.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Separated displacement scales keep unbounded sheet multiplicity uniformly doubling

[Family 098](../families/openai-math-098.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000088.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Take $r_j=1000^{-j}$ and pairs of positive integers $(N_j,W_j)$ in which every pair recurs infinitely often. Above a base point in $\mathbb R^2$, level $j$ permits either zero or $r_je_{j,i}$ in mutually orthogonal directions. Label $i$ is allowed on the union of its periodically colored horizontal strips of width $r_j$ and vertical strips of width $W_jr_j$. Only finitely many levels are nonzero at each point.

Despite unbounded $N_j,W_j$, the resulting Hilbert subset is 76800-doubling. In a ball of radius $t$, levels with $r_j>t$ are fixed. At most one level lies in $(t/64,t]$, where the base projection encounters fewer than 300 labels. The remaining displacement tail has squared diameter at most

$$2\sum_{r_j\le t/64}r_j^2\le\frac{2(t/64)^2}{1-10^{-6}}<(t/32)^2.$$

Partition the base square of side $2t$ into $16^2$ cells of side $t/8$, and group points by cell and intermediate label. Every group has diameter below $\sqrt{33}\,t/32<t/2$. Selecting a center from each nonempty group gives at most $300\cdot16^2$ intrinsic half-radius balls.

## Role in the source argument

Makes room for arbitrarily many recurring branch labels while keeping metric covering complexity uniformly bounded at every radius.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:set](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L106)
- [prop:doubling](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L115)
- [eq:tail](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L124)

## Antecedents and comparison

Multiscale doubling constructions have substantial antecedents, including [Lafforgue–Naor’s Lp obstruction](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~naor/homepage%20files/Lp-doubling.pdf). The particular union of horizontal and vertical permissions is important here because it supplies common sheets at later crossings. The covering argument uses elementary geometric-series and cell counts.

## Checks and limitations

Checked coarse-coordinate rigidity, the single-intermediate-level claim, strip counts and the exact rational tail and diameter bounds. All centers lie in the constructed subset.

This covering estimate alone is no obstruction to finite-dimensional embedding. Recurrence and the shared horizontal/vertical sheet domains are needed by the later derivative argument. The displayed space is not the compact Banach-space example.

## Possible applications

Constructing metric spaces with large combinatorial complexity but bounded local covering counts, provided fine-scale tails and the number of active intermediate labels can both be controlled.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Lexicographic derivative extrema turn crossing sheets into a packing obstruction

[Family 098](../families/openai-math-098.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000088.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Under a proposed bi-Lipschitz embedding of the sheet space into $\mathbb R^k$ with lower constant 1 and upper constant $D$, collect all good-point derivative pairs $(|F_x|^2,|F_y|^2)$ in one compact closure $K\subset[0,D^2]^2$. Let $A$ maximize the first coordinate, and $B$ maximize the second on the first-coordinate face $s=A$. Compactness gives

$$\mathbb E(A-s_n)\to0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\limsup\mathbb E t_n\le B$$

for arbitrary probability-space-valued pairs $(s_n,t_n)\in K$. No quantitative modulus for the second extremum is needed.

Choose fixed $N>(1+2D)^k$ and recurring aspect ratios $W_j=n$. Near $(A,B)$, the source obtains horizontal and vertical selected-sheet errors

$$n^2\langle|G_H^x-F_x|^2\rangle\to0,\qquad
\langle|G_V^y-F_y|^2\rangle\to0.$$

The horizontal estimate has an explicit $O(n^{-2})$ bound after multiplication by $n^2$; the vertical estimate uses only compactness. On one period block of width $Nnr$ and height $Nr$, line selection and Cauchy–Schwarz make normalized offsets vary by at most $\omega_n=N\sqrt{2N\epsilon_n}\to0$. At cross-color intersections two permitted displacements are separated by $\sqrt2r$. Transport along the selected row and column gives $N$ offsets in a radius-D ball, pairwise separated by at least $\sqrt2-2\omega_n>1$. Volume packing contradicts $N>(1+2D)^k$.

## Role in the source argument

Uses a quantitative first-direction estimate to pay for long horizontal lines and a qualitative second-direction estimate for bounded normalized vertical lengths. The same sheet must be used on both arms of each crossing.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:compact](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L177)
- [prop:energy](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L248)
- [eq:Hrate](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L272)
- [eq:omega](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L341)

## Antecedents and comparison

Differentiation and separation-versus-stretch arguments precede this source, notably [Laakso](https://doi.org/10.1007/s000390050003). The elementary lexicographic compactness lemma is not presented as a new compactness principle. The candidate instrument is its asymmetric use with recurring crossed sheets and finite-dimensional packing.

## Checks and limitations

Read the two energy estimates and crossing selection in full. Checked the variance expansion, the endpoint errors divided by strip width, the n-scaling and the final packing count.

The compact set K and target parameters must remain fixed as n grows. Independent horizontal and vertical branch maps would not provide the common crossing values. This mechanism is tied to the supplied geometry; it is not a general assertion about all doubling subsets.

## Possible applications

Designing rigidity arguments with several directional energies when only the first direction admits an effective rate, and isolating the geometric compatibility needed for a packing contradiction.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Finite Hilbert obstructions can be assembled into a compact obstruction in any Banach space

[Family 098](../families/openai-math-098.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000088.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Suppose a fixed Hilbert subset S is lambda-doubling and admits no finite-distortion embedding into any finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Compactness of bounded coordinate products implies that for every target dimension and distortion bound there is a finite witness inside S. Choose $X_j\subset S$ excluding distortion at most j into $\mathbb R^j$.

For any infinite-dimensional real Banach space B, Dvoretzky’s theorem places each finite Hilbert span in B with distortion strictly below 2. Translate and shrink the images into finite clusters $C_j\subset B_B(2^{-j}v,2^{-j}/100)$, where v is a fixed unit vector. Then

$$K_B=\{0\}\cup\bigcup_{j\ge1}C_j$$

is compact, has a universal doubling bound $1+6\lambda^8$, and admits no embedding into any finite-dimensional normed space at any finite distortion.

The individual clusters are at most $\lambda^4$-doubling. For a radius-r ball, clusters at scales at most r/4 fit in one tail ball; at most five larger dyadic scales can meet the ball if more than one such cluster does. Each intersection needs at most $\lambda^8$ half-radius balls. An embedding of K_B with Euclidean target dimension k and distortion D contradicts the witness X_j for any j>=k with j>=2D.

## Role in the source argument

Separates the infinite geometric obstruction from compactness and from the ambient Banach space. The initial noncompact sheet construction supplies finite witnesses; classical finite representability performs the transfer.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [cor:banach](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L418)
- [sec:banach](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-doubling-Hilbert-subset-with-no-finite-dimensional-bi-Lipschitz-embedding-September-25-2026/build/main.tex#L415)

## Antecedents and comparison

Finite-witness compactness and Dvoretzky are classical, not newly proved phenomena. The source explicitly uses only the qualitative finite-dimensional Dvoretzky theorem. Related fixed-set obstructions appear in [Lafforgue–Naor](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~naor/homepage%20files/Lp-doubling.pdf); the present conditional assembly applies to the Hilbert obstruction supplied earlier in the manuscript.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the product-compactness quantifiers, recentering cost in the doubling estimate, dyadic scale count and strict distortion margin. Exact rational checks confirm the tail and cluster-separation constants.

This transfer assumes finite witnesses already exist and gives a very large, nonoptimal doubling constant. It uses completeness of the ambient Banach space through the stated setting and finite-dimensional near-Euclidean representability; no single universal subset is asserted to be isometric in all ambient spaces.

## Possible applications

Turning families of finite metric obstructions into one compact example, while separating source-space placement from target-space impossibility.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Nonlinear Jacobian compatibility forces a linear symmetric matrix field to commute

[Family 101](../families/openai-math-101.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000089.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let $X_1,\ldots,X_m$ be real symmetric m-by-m matrices, $\sum_rX_r^2=I$, and $A(x)=\sum_rx_rX_r$. Put $t(a)=-\log\Phi(-a)$ and $q=t'$, where $\Phi$ is the standard Gaussian distribution function. If $F\in W^{1,2}_{loc}(\mathbb R^m;\mathbb R^m)$ has weak Jacobian $DF=q(A)$ almost everywhere, then an orthogonal change of input and output makes F a product of signed exponential quantile maps, plus a translation:

$$U^TF(Uy)=(\sigma_i t(\sigma_i y_i))_{i=1}^m+w,\qquad \sigma_i\in\{-1,1\}.$$

The local algebra is especially portable. Jacobian compatibility requires $(\partial_rq(A))e_s=(\partial_sq(A))e_r$. Since $q'(0)\ne0$ and $q''(0)\ne0$, its constant term gives $X_re_s=X_se_r$. The linear term then cancels its common leftmost-A factors and gives $[X_r,X_s]x=0$. Thus all coefficients commute. After simultaneous orthogonal diagonalization and rotating the input as well, coefficient symmetry leaves only the ith diagonal entry of the ith coefficient. The sum-of-squares normalization makes it a sign.

The commutation part of this proof uses only analyticity near zero and nonzero first and second derivatives; this is a consequence of the displayed coefficient argument, not a claim that every such scalar function has the exponential-law conclusion.

## Role in the source argument

Classifies the linear matrix fields obtained when higher-chaos slack vanishes in the entropy argument. Applied to Gaussian input, the specified q gives independent mean-one exponentials up to signs and orthogonal transformation, with covariance I.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:linear-jacobian](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-sharp-entropy-bound-and-the-simplex-inequality-for-isotropic-constants-October-5-2026/build/manuscript/rigidity.tex#L13)

# An exponential cone density transfers entropy gaps to isotropic-constant gaps

[Family 101](../families/openai-math-101.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000089.md) · [Batch B003](../../batches/B003/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^n$ with centroid zero, let $\Sigma_K$ be its uniform covariance and define the cone $\mathcal C_K=\{(tx,t):x\in K,t\ge0\}$. The log-concave density

$$f_K(y,t)=\frac{e^{-t}}{n!|K|}\mathbf1_{\mathcal C_K}(y,t)$$

is the law of $(TX,T)$, where X is uniform on K and independently $T\sim\operatorname{Gamma}(n+1,1)$. Consequently

$$h(f_K)=n+1+\log(n!|K|),\qquad
\det\operatorname{Cov}(f_K)=(n+1)^{n+1}(n+2)^n\det\Sigma_K.$$

Thus the entropy-gap inequality $h(f)\ge m+\frac12\log\det\operatorname{Cov}(f)$ in dimension m=n+1 implies, exactly,

$$L_K\le\frac{(n!)^{1/n}}{(n+1)^{(n+1)/(2n)}\sqrt{n+2}},\qquad
L_K^{2n}=\det\Sigma_K/|K|^2.$$

If entropy equality characterizes affine images of independent exponentials, the cone support must be an affine image of the positive orthant. Its unique extreme point forces the translation to vanish; its height-one section is then a simplex. Conversely, the cone over a simplex is a linear image of the orthant and gives equality.

## Role in the source argument

Carries a sharp functional inequality and its equality classification to a sharp geometric bound with the exact dimension shift and factorial constant.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an established reduction. The source explicitly credits the cone construction to Fradelizi–Meyer and its entropy reduction to [Fradelizi–Marín Sola](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.07406), with moment formulas also attributed to Klartag. Its presence in the new source is useful as a reusable bridge, not as evidence of new priority.

## Checks and limitations

Recomputed the normalization, gamma moments, block covariance and determinant. The finite check verifies the simplex covariance determinant and equality constants in several dimensions, including the interval value L=1/sqrt(12).

The transfer is conditional on the entropy theorem and, for the equality conclusion, on its extremizer classification. Neither follows from these gamma-moment calculations. Covariance must be positive definite, so the body is full-dimensional.

## Possible applications

Converting entropy deficits into geometric extremal bounds and tracking equality through homogeneous cone constructions without losing dimension-dependent constants.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# An entropy optimizer preserves the logarithmic Sobolev deficit under change of reference

[Family 093](../families/openai-math-093.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000090.md) · [Batch B004](../../batches/B004/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Use the convention $\operatorname{Ent}_\nu(g^2)\le2R\int|Dg|^2d\nu$, and put $\lambda=1/R$. The source takes $\nu=\mu*\gamma_s$ with compactly supported $\mu$, $s>0$, and $R>\max\{R^P(\nu),s\}$. It constructs a smooth positive normalized optimizer f satisfying $A_\nu f=\lambda f\log f$, where $A_\nu=-\Delta-D\log\nu\cdot D$. Assume additionally that $\nu=e^{-V}$ is log-concave and $K=D^2V$ is bounded. Put $\eta=f^2\nu$, $h=\log f^2$ and $w=Dh$.

For every probability $p=g^2\eta$ with compact smooth g, the relative Fisher information $\mathcal I$ and relative entropy H satisfy the exact identity

$$\mathcal I(p\mid\nu)-2\lambda H(p\mid\nu)
=\mathcal I(p\mid\eta)-2\lambda H(p\mid\eta).$$

Indeed $H(p\mid\nu)=H(p\mid\eta)+\int h\,dp$, while the Euler equation and integration by parts give $\mathcal I(p\mid\nu)=\mathcal I(p\mid\eta)+2\lambda\int h\,dp$. Hence $R(\eta)\le R$ even though log-concavity of eta is not assumed. The relative score also obeys $A_\eta w=(\lambda I-K)w$ and

$$\mathbb E_\eta\langle w,Kw\rangle\le\lambda|\mathbb E_\eta w|^2.$$

The latter follows by combining the score energy identity with Poincaré under eta.

## Role in the source argument

Turns an entropy extremizer into a new reference measure with the same available entropy coefficient, making its relative score accessible to spectral and prediction estimates.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

## Antecedents and comparison

The surrounding conjecture and earlier dimension-dependent bounds are discussed by [Bizeul](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.12997). Priority for this exact optimizer formulation has not been established by the targeted comparison.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the two change-of-reference expansions and the sign of the weighted divergence. The bundled Gaussian-tilt calculation verifies the deficit identity in a simple equality model; that model is not a test of the strict optimizer-existence hypotheses.

The optimizer and its operator-domain properties are substantial inputs. An arbitrary positive tilt does not preserve the deficit. The extraction does not assume that the tilted measure is log-concave or reconstruct the source’s existence proof.

## Possible applications

Studying equality and near-equality in entropy inequalities through the tilted law, or testing whether an extremal score is close to the first spectral subspace.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Symmetric-slot averaging compares tensor actions with a geometric trace weight

[Family 093](../families/openai-math-093.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000090.md) · [Batch B004](../../batches/B004/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let psi be a finite direct sum of real symmetric tensors, each having at least k slots, with integer $k\ge2$. Its one-slot reduction is the positive matrix rho obtained by flattening one slot against all remaining slots and summing across components; no unit normalization is required. Write $R=\sqrt\rho$. For a self-adjoint matrix H, let $H_{av}$ average its action over the slots of each component. Then

$$\|H_{av}\psi\|^2\le\operatorname{tr}(RHRH)+\frac2k\operatorname{tr}(\rho H^2).$$

For a d-slot component define $a_d=\langle\psi_d,H_{(1)}^2\psi_d\rangle$ and $c_d=\langle\psi_d,H_{(1)}H_{(2)}\psi_d\rangle$. Expansion gives $a_d/d+(1-1/d)c_d$, and $|c_d|\le a_d$ accounts for the 2/k error. The remaining estimate is $|\sum_dc_d|\le\operatorname{tr}(RHRH)$.

The proof expresses the two-slot correlations by a positive map C with $C(I)=C^*(I)=\rho$. Conjugating by rho on its support yields a unital rho-preserving map. Interpolation between its operator-norm and trace-norm endpoint contractions gives the weighted Hilbert–Schmidt contraction producing the geometric trace weight.

## Role in the source argument

Long symmetric tensors make average slot actions close to the geometric matrix energy. In the source this helps convert tensor near-equalities into commutator and square-root-energy control.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:matrix-copied-slots](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-dimension-free-logarithmic-Sobolev-inequality-for-subgaussian-log-concave-measures-September-23-2026/build/sections/06-matrices.tex#L114)
- [eq:matrix-copied-slots](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-dimension-free-logarithmic-Sobolev-inequality-for-subgaussian-log-concave-measures-September-23-2026/build/sections/06-matrices.tex#L119)

## Antecedents and comparison

The source explicitly says its correlation bound also follows from the Wigner–Yanase case of [Lieb’s trace-concavity theorem](https://www.numdam.org/item/RCP25_1973__19__A4_0/). Its alternative proof uses the weighted Schatten interpolation framework of [Beigi](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.5920v6). The classical correlation inequality is not counted as a new theorem; the averaging formulation exposes its role in a tensor hierarchy.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the expansion by equal and unequal slots, the support restriction and the interpolation endpoints. Finite symmetric-tensor examples test both the correlation bound and the final averaging estimate, including singular reductions and direct sums.

Total symmetry is essential to the common one-slot reduction and cross-slot expansion. The trace is unnormalized. The 2/k error is part of the statement and cannot be dropped merely because the ambient dimension is large.

## Possible applications

Comparing many-body symmetric tensors with one-body matrix energies, and importing quantum trace inequalities into classical analytic near-equality arguments.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Scale-integrated covariance maps are Lipschitz in Hilbert–Schmidt distance

[Family 093](../families/openai-math-093.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000090.md) · [Batch B004](../../batches/B004/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix $L\ge1$, define $f_L(q)=q/(1+q/L)$ for q>=0, and set $h_T(v)=\sqrt{1+f_L(Tv^2)}$. For arbitrary positive semidefinite matrices A and B of the same size, including noncommuting and singular ones,

$$\int_0^\infty\|h_T(A)-h_T(B)\|_F^2\frac{dT}{T^2}
\le K_L\|A-B\|_F^2,$$

where

$$K_L=\int_0^\infty\frac{dq}{(1+q/L)^3(1+(1+1/L)q)},\qquad0<K_L\le\log(1+L).$$

For v>0, differentiating and substituting q=Tv^2 gives exactly $\int_0^\infty|h_T'(v)|^2dT/T^2=K_L$, independent of v. The fundamental theorem of calculus, Cauchy–Schwarz and Tonelli give the scalar Lipschitz bound, also at zero. Using separate eigenbases for A and B turns it into the matrix estimate by summing scalar bounds weighted by squared eigenvector overlaps. Simultaneous diagonalization is unnecessary.

## Role in the source argument

Controls Gaussian covariance observations across every scale, allowing replacement of a square-root matrix field by its limiting model without losing contributions from small spectral blocks. Coupling with the same Gaussian noise makes the mean squared observation difference exactly the matrix Frobenius difference.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:obs-integrated-stability](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-dimension-free-logarithmic-Sobolev-inequality-for-subgaussian-log-concave-measures-September-23-2026/build/sections/07-observations.tex#L202)
- [eq:obs-matrix-stability](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/A-dimension-free-logarithmic-Sobolev-inequality-for-subgaussian-log-concave-measures-September-23-2026/build/sections/07-observations.tex#L210)

## Antecedents and comparison

The eigenbasis argument is the standard Frobenius functional-calculus mechanism, also visible in the source of [MI-000133](MI-000133.md). The scale-integrated derivative identity for this bounded covariance map is the particular extracted estimate. Targeted comparison has not established its historical novelty.

## Checks and limitations

Differentiated h_T, checked the scale substitution and read the separate-eigenbasis proof. Numerical quadrature tests singular and noncommuting positive matrices against K_L and the logarithmic upper bound.

The result is in Hilbert–Schmidt norm, not an arbitrary operator norm. L is held fixed when applying a convergence argument. Numerical quadrature is not a proof of the universal inequality; that follows from the displayed scalar calculation and eigenbasis reduction.

## Possible applications

Comparing matrix-valued observations uniformly over scales and preserving trace mass when the spectrum becomes diffuse.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Deletion and Gaussian translation bracket the loss of a winning score

[Family 096](../families/openai-math-096.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000091.md) · [Batch B004](../../batches/B004/README.md)

## Mathematical content

In the source’s optimal partition with the fewest active cells, let $z_1,\ldots,z_m$ be the nonzero Gaussian first moments, $C=\sum_i|z_i|^2$, $X_i=\langle z_i,g\rangle$, $r_i=|z_i|/\sqrt C$, $P_i=\Pr(X_i=\max_jX_j)$ and $\alpha=m/(m-1)$. Under its putative-counterexample reduction, m>=5, the centroids sum to zero, have negative pairwise inner products, and span dimension m-1. The expected loss from deleting score i satisfies

$$C(1-\sqrt{1-\alpha r_i^2})
\le\mathbb E(X_i-\max_{j\ne i}X_j)_+
\le\alpha\phi(q)\bigl(q\Phi(q)+\phi(q)\bigr),\quad q=\Phi^{-1}(P_i).$$

The lower bound deletes z_i, recenters the remaining list and uses the extremal Gaussian-maximum inequality; its remaining squared norm is $C-\alpha|z_i|^2$. For the upper bound, choose h with $\langle h,z_i-z_j\rangle=1$ for every j!=i. The winning cone K_i has gap tail $p_i(u)=\gamma(K_i+uh)$ and derivative $p_i'(0)=-\langle h,z_i\rangle=-1/\alpha$. Ehrhard concavity makes $\Phi^{-1}(p_i(u))$ lie below its tangent at zero. Integrating the resulting Gaussian tail gives the upper bound.

## Role in the source argument

Converts deletion optimality into a lower bound on a cell’s probability relative to its normalized centroid radius. This supplements rearrangement estimates in the finite-dimensional elimination.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [ext:structure](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/extremizers.tex#L91)
- [sc:loss-lower](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/scalars.tex#L118)
- [sc:translation-derivative](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/scalars.tex#L136)
- [sc:loss-upper](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/scalars.tex#L158)

## Antecedents and comparison

[Khot–Naor](https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.4626) already provide the Gaussian maximum/partition framework. Ehrhard’s Gaussian Minkowski inequality is an established input; the source derives the particular translating vector and deletion bracket. The separate [three-dimensional propeller theorem](https://arxiv.org/abs/1112.2993) is also an input, not newly extracted as an all-dimensional proof.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the recentered norm, the basis needed to solve for h, the sign and normalization of the translated-measure derivative, and the integrated tangent formula. The bundled calculation tests the exact recentering identity and Gaussian-tail integral.

Optimality and the self-consistency between winning cones and their actual first moments are necessary. Arbitrary Gaussian score vectors need not obey this bracket. Checking the bracket does not reproduce the source’s later numerical certificates or prove the global propeller bound.

## Possible applications

Turning removal or pruning operations in Gaussian optimization into quantitative mass constraints by combining a variational lower bound with a translated-set upper bound.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Zero residual moments turn two-score competition into a determinant bound

[Family 096](../families/openai-math-096.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000091.md) · [Batch B004](../../batches/B004/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Continue with the minimal-active-cell optimal partition under the assumption $C>9/(8\pi)$ and m>=5. Choose the smallest normalized centroid radius $t=|z_m|/\sqrt C$, let $e=z_m/|z_m|$, and put

$$a_j=-\frac{\langle z_m,z_j\rangle}{|z_m|^2}>0,\quad\sum_{j<m}a_j=1,\qquad
w_j=z_j/\sqrt C+a_jte.$$

The residual scores $Y_j=\langle w_j,g\rangle$ are independent of $T=\langle e,g\rangle\sim N(0,1)$. For the covariance H of these residuals, let $D_{jk}=\sqrt{H_{jj}H_{kk}-H_{jk}^2}>0$. Then

$$D_{jk}\le\frac3\pi\,t(1+a_j)(1+a_k)\qquad(j\ne k<m).$$

On the winning cell K of z_m, $T\ge0$, $Y_j\le(1+a_j)tT$, and $\mathbb E[1_KY_j]=0$. Normalize $U=Y_j/((1+a_j)t)$ and $V=Y_k/((1+a_k)t)$. Their joint density is bounded by $M=t^2(1+a_j)(1+a_k)/(2\pi D_{jk})$. Adding their zero first moments and taking a positive part bounds $\mathbb E[1_KT]$ by

$$M\,\mathbb E\int_{u\le T,v\le T}(T+u+v)_+\,du\,dv
=\frac{27M}{6}\mathbb E T_+^3.$$

Here the integral is taken for T>=0 and is zero otherwise; its value for T=s>=0 is $(3s)^3/6$. Comparing with $\mathbb E[1_KT]=\sqrt C\,t>3t/(2\sqrt{2\pi})$ yields the determinant estimate.

## Role in the source argument

Links a small winning centroid to the area scale of every pair of residual competitors. Negative off-diagonal covariances then prevent all relevant determinants from being small simultaneously.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [geo:pair](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/geometry.tex#L63)
- [geo:centroid-identities](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/geometry.tex#L79)
- [geo:density-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Gaussian-Propeller-Bound-in-Every-Dimension-September-24-2026/build/sections/geometry.tex#L95)

## Antecedents and comparison

Residual orthogonal projection, Gaussian independence and density-max bounds are classical. The candidate combination uses exact zero residual moments to integrate over a bounded triangle rather than an unbounded two-score region. Its surrounding conical optimization is inherited from [Khot–Naor](https://arxiv.org/abs/0807.4626).

## Checks and limitations

Recomputed the covariance determinant under scaling and the triangle integral exactly, and checked the Gaussian third positive moment and final constant 3/pi.

The positive determinant uses linear independence of proper subsets of the extremal centroids. The claimed inequality is conditional on the source’s counterexample setup and is used to eliminate it; it is not a constraint on all centered Gaussian covariance matrices.

## Possible applications

Bounding residual covariance through constrained first moments, especially when several zero-moment identities can be added to make a positive-part integration region bounded.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Diagonal spectral energy supports signs with bounded adaptive shifts

[Family 097](../families/openai-math-097.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000092.md) · [Batch B004](../../batches/B004/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let K be nonempty, bounded, open, convex and symmetric about zero in $\mathbb R^m$. For positive diagonal Q let $\lambda_Q(K)$ be the first Dirichlet Rayleigh infimum $\inf\int\langle Q\nabla g,\nabla g\rangle/\int g^2$. Assume

$$\lambda_Q(K)\le\kappa^2\operatorname{tr}Q\quad\text{for every such Q},\qquad\kappa=1/100.$$

For distinct coordinate indices $j_1,\ldots,j_s$ and arbitrary functions $q_i:\mathbb R^{i-1}\to[-1/4,1/4]$, signs exist for which the successive coordinate assignments $x_{j_i}=q_i(x_{j_1},\ldots,x_{j_{i-1}})+\epsilon_i$, with all unassigned coordinates zero, end at a point in K.

The energy hypothesis first produces one normalized nonnegative f supported in K with $\int|\partial_i f|^2\le\kappa^2$ for every i. Convexity of coordinate-energy upper bounds follows from mixing densities and taking square roots; separation uses every positive diagonal Q. A lifted Steiner construction then supplies a domain $T_e(K)$ with the same spectral bounds such that every y in it, for every |q|<=1/4, has one of $y+(q\pm1)e$ in K. Its height estimate is $(\ell/2)(1-2\ell\kappa)=19/16>1$ for $\ell=5/2$. Backward domain transforms followed by forward sign choices accommodate the adaptive shifts.

## Role in the source argument

Allows each coefficient to contain a small causal correction as well as a sign. This extra freedom is exactly what the contraction-canceling predictor needs.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

The cited Akbas–Sra version is dated September 29; the source’s filename date alone is not a priority chronology.

# Causal predictor columns cancel rank-one contractions at a telescoping energy cost

[Family 097](../families/openai-math-097.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000092.md) · [Batch B004](../../batches/B004/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For Euclidean unit-ball vectors $v_i$, choose $0<\sigma<1$, put $b_i=\sigma v_i$, $\eta_i=(1+\sqrt{1-|b_i|^2})^{-1}$ and $C_i=I-\eta_ib_ib_i^T=(I-b_ib_i^T)^{1/2}$. Define coefficient-to-state maps by $R_0x=x_{1:d}$ and $R_ix=C_iR_{i-1}x+b_ix_{d+i}$. Let $x^0$ zero the first d coordinates, and let the predictor rows be $m_ix=\eta_ib_i^TR_{i-1}x^0$.

These rows involve only earlier noise coordinates. If M is their matrix, every column satisfies $|Me_j|^2\le\sigma^2$. For a column injected as b_j, follow $r_i=C_ir_{i-1}$ after its injection; the exact loss $|r_{i-1}|^2-|r_i|^2=(b_i^Tr_{i-1})^2$ telescopes. Since $\eta_i\le1$, it bounds the sum of squared predictor coefficients. Hence

$$\sum_i m_iQm_i^T\le\sigma^2\operatorname{tr}Q$$

for every positive diagonal Q, independently of the sequence length.

If a final coefficient vector has zero initial block and $x_{d+i}=m_ix+\epsilon_i$, then $R_ix=R_{i-1}x+\epsilon_ib_i$ exactly, so all filtered states are the signed prefixes. The source chooses clipped adaptive shifts and imposes final slabs |m_ix|<1/4; causality then proves that clipping was inactive at every assignment.

## Role in the source argument

Connects the adaptive spectral-signing criterion to the separately controlled filtered path body. The small column cost makes all predictor slabs affordable, and cancellation removes the artificial contraction from the final signed walk.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [eq:predictor-columns](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Euclidean-Steinitz-Bergstrom-theorem-September-24-2026/build/assembly.tex#L163)
- [eq:unclipped-coordinates](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-Euclidean-Steinitz-Bergstrom-theorem-September-24-2026/build/assembly.tex#L217)

## Antecedents and comparison

Rank-one square-root filters, feedback cancellation and telescoping energy identities are elementary established techniques. The source’s candidate assembly combines them with adaptive spectral signing to obtain simultaneous prefixes. The geometric signing antecedents are [Guo–Fang–Lu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11189v1) and [Akbas–Sra](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.27172v2).

## Checks and limitations

Finite examples with noncommuting consecutive contractions check the square-root identity, column-energy budgets, causal support and simultaneous cancellation. Zero vectors are included.

The algebra does not by itself produce a bounded signed walk: the length-independent energy estimate for the filtered path body and the adaptive-sign existence theorem remain essential inputs. Final slab membership must be established before removing the clipping operation.

## Possible applications

Building rounding schemes in which a stable auxiliary dynamics is canceled by small causal corrections whose total coordinate cost can be bounded by an energy loss.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Finite response bounds extend by limsup to a canonical infinite-volume drift

[Family 231](../families/openai-math-231.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000093.md) · [Batch B005](../../batches/B005/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a finite weighted spanning-tree law with log weights h and inclusion means p, differentiation gives $\partial_{h_f}p_e=\operatorname{Cov}(X_e,X_f)$. Negative off-diagonal covariances and the fixed tree size yield

$$\sum_f|\partial_{h_f}p_e|=2p_e(1-p_e)\le\tfrac12.$$

For a general finite strongly Rayleigh binary law the equality becomes an inequality. Exponential tilting preserves that property, so the same uniform response bound holds at every finite field. This covariance estimate is an established input.

For the free uniform spanning forest law nu and finite edge set S, define

$$b_{e,S}(t,y)=\frac{\mathbb E_\nu[X_e\exp\{\sum_{f\in S}(y_f-t/2)X_f\}]}{\mathbb E_\nu[\exp\{\sum_{f\in S}(y_f-t/2)X_f\}]}.$$

The denominator is positive. A free finite-graph limit, taken with S fixed, preserves the response bound. Let $S_n(e)$ be the edges induced by the vertices within distance n of either endpoint of e, and set $b_e(t,y)=\limsup_n b_{e,S_n(e)}(t,y)$. This produces a jointly Borel, root-free, isomorphism-equivariant drift on all real edge fields, with values in $[0,1]$, and

$$\sup_e|b_e(t,y)-b_e(t,y')|\le\tfrac12\sup_f|y_f-y'_f|$$

whenever the right side is finite. Neither field is required to be bounded. Taking the two limsup inequalities in opposite directions proves the estimate. The outer limsup need not be a limit on arbitrary inputs; along the observation process it agrees almost surely at each fixed time with the posterior mean.

## Role in the source argument

Makes a posterior drift available on every path input without defining an infinite-volume partition function or imposing a bounded-field state space.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:tree-response](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/build/sections/response.tex#L14)
- [eq:finite-tilt](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/build/sections/response.tex#L216)
- [prop:canonical-drift](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/build/sections/response.tex#L276)
- [lem:sr-response](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/build/sections/strongly-rayleigh.tex#L14)

## Antecedents and comparison

The row bound is already stated in [Alishahi, Barzegar and Zamani, Lemma 2.5 and equation (1)](https://arxiv.org/html/2203.03935v2), following earlier work of [Ghosh, Liggett and Pemantle](https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.03036v1). The extracted construction combines that input with fixed-field forest limits and an intrinsic outer limsup; the classical bound is not a new result.

## Checks and limitations

Read the finite matrix-tree response proof, the strongly Rayleigh homogenization argument, and the two ordered spatial limits. Exact rational enumeration checks weighted tree covariances, including bridges; finite determinant examples check the nonhomogeneous covariance inequality.

The order of limits matters: first the finite-graph limit with S fixed, then the limsup over S. Negative pairwise correlations alone do not supply the row bound. Equivariant exhaustions or another equivariant drift construction are needed for a factor conclusion.

## Possible applications

Constructing globally defined posterior drifts for other negatively dependent infinite-volume laws, with the finite response estimate as a reusable criterion.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Picard inversion on the full product path space gives a Brownian sampler

[Family 231](../families/openai-math-231.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000093.md) · [Batch B005](../../batches/B005/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let I be countable. Suppose $b:[0,\infty)\times\mathbb R^I\to[0,1]^I$ is jointly Borel and satisfies $\|b(t,y)-b(t,y')\|_\infty\le L\|y-y'\|_\infty$ whenever the difference is bounded. Every input $w\in\prod_i C([0,\infty),\mathbb R)$ then has a unique solution

$$Z_i(w)(t)=w_i(t)+\int_0^t b_i(s,Z(w)(s))\,ds.$$

Starting with $Z^0=w$, the Picard increments obey

$$\sup_i|Z_i^{k+1}(t)-Z_i^k(t)|\le \frac{L^kt^{k+1}}{(k+1)!}.$$

These summable majorants control differences uniformly over coordinates and compact time intervals. They do not bound w itself or require a common coordinate modulus of continuity. Parameterized integration and rational-time evaluations give a Borel causal solution map; it inherits every equivariance of b.

For a binary law nu, form finite posterior tilts as in MI-000142 along finite exhaustions of I. If these are uniformly L-Lipschitz, their limsup drift satisfies the hypotheses. In the planted model $Y_i(t)=tX_i+B_i(t)$, $X\sim\nu$, the innovations $W_i=Y_i-\int_0^t b_i(s,Y(s))ds$ have joint product Wiener law. Deterministic uniqueness gives $Y=Z(W)$. Hence

$$\Psi_i(w)=\mathbf1\{\limsup_{n\to\infty}Z_i(w)(n)/n>1/2\}$$

is a Borel sampler with full configuration law nu. Gaussian tails and a countable Borel-Cantelli argument identify all integer-time slopes simultaneously.

## Role in the source argument

Converts a dimension-free posterior response estimate into a measurable sampling rule from independent noise, preserving the symmetries of the target law.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:inverse](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/build/sections/decoder.tex#L13)
- [eq:picard-bound](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/build/sections/decoder.tex#L46)
- [prop:brownian-sampler](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/build/sections/decoder.tex#L101)
- [lem:innovation](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-free-uniform-spanning-forest-is-a-factor-of-IID-September-25-2026/build/sections/observation.tex#L88)

## Antecedents and comparison

Picard iteration and Brownian innovations are classical. [Nam, Sly and Zhang](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.09484v2) already construct Ising factors through an infinite-dimensional Brownian observation equation. The particular reusable feature here is an everywhere-defined inverse on the unrestricted product path space, under a uniform finite-tilt response criterion. This is not an assertion that Brownian posterior sampling originated in the release.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the factorial induction, uniqueness relative to the same unbounded input, and law transfer through the reference observation model. Finite quadrature examples exercise the Picard majorants, with discretization error reported separately.

Uniform finite-tilt response is a substantive assumption. This is an exact existence criterion, not a finite-time approximation guarantee. Integer-time slope recovery is an infinite-time operation.

## Possible applications

Sampling invariant binary fields and testing whether a finite-dimensional sensitivity estimate suffices for an infinite-volume IID factor.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Weak convergence plus support-edge convergence controls the capped R-transform uniformly

[Family 234](../families/openai-math-234.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000094.md) · [Batch B005](../../batches/B005/README.md)

## Mathematical content

For a probability tau supported in $[-K,K]$, let $e_\tau=\max\operatorname{supp}\tau$ and $H_\tau(z)=\int(z-\lambda)^{-1}d\tau(\lambda)$ for $z>e_\tau$. For x>0, define $b_\tau(x)$ as the unique solution of $H_\tau(b)=x$ above the edge when it exists, and otherwise set $b_\tau(x)=e_\tau$. Put $R_\tau(x)=b_\tau(x)-1/x$ and $R_\tau(0)=\int\lambda\,d\tau$.

If $\nu_j\Rightarrow\nu$, all supports lie in a common bounded interval, and $e_{\nu_j}\to e_\nu$, then

$$\sup_{0\le x\le1}|R_{\nu_j}(x)-R_\nu(x)|\longrightarrow0.$$

Away from zero, subsequences of inverse values are compact. Limits above the edge obey the inverse equation; a hypothetical wrong edge limit is excluded by evaluating H at a fixed intermediate point. Near zero the uniform estimate

$$R_\tau(x)=\int\lambda\,d\tau+O(K^2x)$$

completes the argument. It follows by expanding $1=\int[1+x(R_\tau(x)-\lambda)]^{-1}d\tau$, using $|R_\tau|\le K$ and $x<(4K)^{-1}$.

For the source functional $\mathcal F(\nu)=\inf_p[S(p)+\tfrac12\int_0^1R_\nu(D_p(r))dr]$, where the common admissible class, S and $0\le D_p\le1$ do not depend on nu, this gives

$$|\mathcal F(\nu_j)-\mathcal F(\nu)|\le\tfrac12\|R_{\nu_j}-R_\nu\|_\infty.$$

No density regularity near the edge is assumed.

## Role in the source argument

Allows approximation by finite spectral alphabets while retaining the edge-capped branch of the variational term.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [gen:R-continuity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/build/60-general.tex#L18)
- [gen:R-at-zero](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/build/60-general.tex#L90)
- [gen:variational-continuity](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/build/60-general.tex#L31)

## Antecedents and comparison

The transform and its edge-sensitive role in spherical integrals belong to the framework of [Guionnet and Maida](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0406121v3). [Fan and Wu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.02797v3) study the corresponding invariant Ising setting in the replica-symmetric regime. This card isolates the source’s compactness-and-origin argument, without claiming a new R-transform theory or established priority for the lemma.

## Checks and limitations

Checked both inverse branches and the uniform origin remainder. Computations test atomic approximations and the scalar transform equation. A vanishing-mass distant atom is a negative control showing why support-edge convergence cannot simply be omitted.

The shared support bound and convergence of the upper edges are explicit hypotheses. The conclusion does not by itself prove that the variational functional equals thermodynamic pressure.

## Possible applications

Passing from finite alphabets to rough compact spectral laws in variational problems with edge-capped Stieltjes inverses.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Eigenspace symmetry bounds pressure changes caused by spectral multiplicity errors

[Family 234](../families/openai-math-234.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000094.md) · [Batch B005](../../batches/B005/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Fix distinct real eigenvalues $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m$ with diameter $L=\max\lambda_a-\min\lambda_a$. Let diagonal spectra Lambda and tilde-Lambda have positive integer multiplicities $k_a,\widetilde k_a$, both summing to N. For Haar orthogonal U and any fixed probability prior rho on $\{-1,1\}^N$, set

$$P_N(\Lambda,U)=N^{-1}\log\sum_\sigma\rho(\sigma)\exp\{\tfrac12(U\sigma)^T\Lambda(U\sigma)\}.$$

Then

$$|\mathbb EP_N(\Lambda,U)-\mathbb EP_N(\widetilde\Lambda,U)|
\le\frac L2\max_a\frac{|k_a-\widetilde k_a|}{\min(k_a,\widetilde k_a)}.$$

Arrange the spectra to retain $\min(k_a,\widetilde k_a)$ axes at each eigenvalue, and interpolate by Delta=tilde-Lambda minus Lambda. Convexity bounds the pressure difference between the two endpoint derivatives. At either endpoint, Haar row rotations make expected Gibbs squared projections equal within each eigenspace. A group with q axes, c of which change, therefore contributes the fraction c/q of its total expected squared norm. The total is N, and each changed eigenvalue moves by at most L, proving the bound. Deterministic external fields can be absorbed into the fixed prior.

## Role in the source argument

Controls rounding errors in positive spectral proportions even when the aligned matrices are not close in operator norm.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [gen:counts](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/build/60-general.tex#L127)
- [gen:count-comparison](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/All-temperature-pressure-for-orthogonally-invariant-Ising-spin-glasses-September-25-2026/build/60-general.tex#L133)

## Antecedents and comparison

Convex interpolation and rotational invariance are established tools in invariant spin glasses; see [Bhattacharya and Sen](https://arxiv.org/abs/1507.05067v2) and [Fan and Wu](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.02797v3). The extracted estimate packages endpoint eigenspace symmetry into a relative multiplicity bound. Targeted searches did not establish its historical priority.

## Checks and limitations

Read the alignment and endpoint derivative proof. Finite permutation averaging inside equal-eigenvalue blocks verifies the changed-axis fraction and derivative bound for arbitrary fixed Gibbs weights, including an external-field prior.

This is an expectation under Haar rotation, not a pointwise bound for each U. Every listed multiplicity is positive; a small number of new outlier eigenvalues is not covered by a vanishing relative-error conclusion.

## Possible applications

Removing rational-proportion restrictions in finite-alphabet spectral models and handling deterministic rounding in invariant random-matrix variational arguments.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Compatible conditional copies turn innovation uniqueness into measurable recovery

[Family 236](../families/openai-math-236.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000095.md) · [Batch B005](../../batches/B005/README.md)

## Mathematical content

Let X be the source’s countable continuous observation array and W its causal innovations, which form independent Brownian coordinates relative to the observation history. Disintegrate the joint path law as $K(w,dx)\,\mathsf w(dw)$ and, conditional on the entire W path, sample two independent copies $X^1,X^2$ from K.

The necessary compatibility identity is

$$\mathbb E[F(X_{\le t})\mid W]=\mathbb E[F(X_{\le t})\mid W_{\le t}]$$

for bounded past functionals F. Future W increments are independent of the original observation past, and W up to t is a function of that past. The identity implies that W remains Brownian in the joint past filtration of the two copies. Equations involving stochastic integrals are transported using causal elementary approximations, the Itô isometry and maximal $L^2$ convergence; equal pair laws alone are not a substitute for this step.

If an applicable comparison proves $X^1=X^2$ almost surely, then for each coordinate v and rational q,

$$\mathbb E[(X_v^1(q)-X_v^2(q))^2\mid W]=2\operatorname{Var}(X_v(q)\mid W)=0.$$

The countably many evaluations determine continuous paths, so K is almost surely a point mass. Integrating rational evaluations against K and taking dyadic piecewise-linear limits gives a Borel recovery map $X=F(W)$, with a fixed default on exceptional inputs. In the Ising observation law $X_v(t)=t\sigma_v+B_v(t)$, integer-time slopes then recover every spin almost surely.

## Role in the source argument

Provides a rigorous route from equality of two specially coupled observations to an IID factor, including the filtration condition needed to compare their stochastic equations.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [prop:compatible-copies](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-sharp-factor-of-IID-threshold-for-the-free-Ising-model-on-regular-trees-September-26-2026/build/sections/05-coupling.tex#L67)
- [eq:past-compatibility](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-sharp-factor-of-IID-threshold-for-the-free-Ising-model-on-regular-trees-September-26-2026/build/sections/05-coupling.tex#L97)
- [eq:copy-coordinate-variance](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-sharp-factor-of-IID-threshold-for-the-free-Ising-model-on-regular-trees-September-26-2026/build/sections/05-coupling.tex#L222)
- [prop:factor-extraction](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-sharp-factor-of-IID-threshold-for-the-free-Ising-model-on-regular-trees-September-26-2026/build/sections/08b-recovery.tex#L86)

## Antecedents and comparison

This is an application of the established compatible-coupling and strong-solution framework of [Kurtz](https://arxiv.org/html/1305.6747v2), especially the conditional point-mass principle and joint compatibility lemmas. [Nam, Sly and Zhang](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.09484v2) already use Brownian observation equations for Ising IID factors. The release’s detailed path recovery is not presented here as a new general Yamada-Watanabe theorem.

## Checks and limitations

Checked the future-increment independence argument, transport by elementary stochastic integrals, and rational-coordinate recovery. A finite conditional-kernel calculation tests the variance identity and includes a non-Dirac negative control.

Equality of the copies must be proved; it is not supplied by disintegration. The innovations must be Brownian relative to the full observation past. The source’s pointwise equivariance upgrade is a separate local symmetrization argument, not an uncountable intersection of almost-sure events.

## Possible applications

Testing whether an equivariant observation model can be decoded from independent innovations once a suitable conditional-copy uniqueness estimate is available.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.

# Small-field gains and an adaptive path cutoff make a critical Osgood estimate integrable

[Family 236](../families/openai-math-236.md) · [Source manuscript](../papers/P-000095.md) · [Batch B005](../../batches/B005/README.md)

## Mathematical content

At the critical tree parameter $b=d-1\ge2$, $\theta=b^{-1/2}$, let $V(t)=\mathbb E(\Delta h_o(t))^2$ for the compatible copies. On a finite horizon assume the source’s established comparison inputs: V is absolutely continuous, $V(0)=0$, $0\le V\le H^2$, and its weighted path estimates hold. Write $K>\max(1,H^2)$, $I=1+\log(K/V)$ when V>0, and $\omega=\min(\sqrt t,1)$.

For $a(z)=(1-\tanh^2z)/(1-\theta^2\tanh^2z)$, put $S=\mathbb E[\log a(Y)-\log a(Y')]^2$ using corresponding cavity fields. The source supplies $\mathbb E|Y-Y'|^2\le CV$, a deterministic difference bound, and the marginal tail $\Pr(|Y|>t^{1/8})\le \exp[-c\log^2(1/t)]$. Because $|(\log a)'(z)|\le2|\tanh z|$, splitting small and large fields gives

$$S\le C_TV\left(t^{1/4}+\frac{I}{\log^2(1/t)}\right),\qquad S\le CV.$$

The exceptional contribution is bounded by $\min(CV,C_Te^{-c\log^2(1/t)})$; a split according to whether $V\le e^{-c\log^2(1/t)/2}$ proves the logarithmic gain without independence of Y and Y'.

The weighted path inputs are $Q_r\le CrS$, $L_r\le V$, and, for $r\ge C_0/\omega$, exponentially damped versions with errors $C_Tr^2e^{-\alpha b^{\gamma r}}$ and $C_Te^{-\alpha b^{\gamma r}}$. Choosing

$$R=\left\lceil C_1(\omega^{-1}+\log I)\right\rceil$$

absorbs the double-exponential tails beyond R into V-squared times a summable sequence. Consequently

$$\sum Q_r\le C_T[S(\omega^{-2}+\log^2 I)+V^2],$$
$$\sum\sqrt{Q_r}\le C_T[\sqrt S(\omega^{-3/2}+(\log I)^{3/2})+V],$$
$$\sum L_r\le C_T[V(\omega^{-1}+\log I)+V^2].$$

Inserting these in the source’s variance bound $V'\le C(V+\sum Q_r+\sum L_r+\sqrt V\sum\sqrt{Q_r})$ yields $V'\le k_T(t)V[1+\log(K/V)]$, where for sufficiently small $t\le t_*\le e^{-1}$ one can take

$$k_T(t)=C_T\left(1+t^{-3/4}+\frac1{t\log^2(1/t)}\right),$$

and k is bounded later. This is integrable at zero. The Osgood integral diverges at V=0, forcing $V\equiv0$. The small-field gain specifically replaces the nonintegrable term V/t that the coarse estimate S<=CV would leave.

## Role in the source argument

Isolates the analytic mechanism used at the threshold, where the tree’s branching growth cancels the squared correlation decay and a direct Gronwall bound is insufficient.

## Source locations

The statement is extracted from OpenAI's source manuscript at revision `1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a`. These links identify the exact labelled passages; the batch source manifest records their hashes.

- [lem:small-log-loss](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-sharp-factor-of-IID-threshold-for-the-free-Ising-model-on-regular-trees-September-26-2026/build/sections/08-critical-comparison.tex#L208)
- [eq:variance-cutoff](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-sharp-factor-of-IID-threshold-for-the-free-Ising-model-on-regular-trees-September-26-2026/build/sections/08-critical-comparison.tex#L296)
- [lem:cutoff-sums](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-sharp-factor-of-IID-threshold-for-the-free-Ising-model-on-regular-trees-September-26-2026/build/sections/08-critical-comparison.tex#L318)
- [eq:integrable-osgood](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-sharp-factor-of-IID-threshold-for-the-free-Ising-model-on-regular-trees-September-26-2026/build/sections/08-critical-comparison.tex#L427)
- [eq:osgood-coefficient](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/1581d4cbdd69a0faf34b2089614fe2a814316a6a/preprints/The-sharp-factor-of-IID-threshold-for-the-free-Ising-model-on-regular-trees-September-26-2026/build/sections/08-critical-comparison.tex#L437)

## Antecedents and comparison

Osgood uniqueness and exponential path summation are classical. The earlier [Nam-Sly-Zhang construction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.09484v2) supplies the Brownian Ising-factor setting below a constant multiple of the reconstruction scale. The candidate refinement here is the particular small-field gain, discrepancy-dependent cutoff and integrable critical coefficient. Targeted comparison does not establish priority for all components.

## Checks and limitations

Read the moment-to-tail argument, small-log-loss split, three path sums and final absolutely continuous comparison. Scalar tests check the bad-event bound and cutoff absorption in logarithmic coordinates; exact integral formulas verify the displayed coefficient is integrable.

The preceding critical information and weighted path estimates are substantial hypotheses, not consequences of this scalar calculation. These selected checks do not certify the full sharp threshold theorem or arbitrary-solution pathwise uniqueness.

## Possible applications

Other critical stochastic comparisons in which a coarse 1/t divergence can be improved using a vanishing derivative at typical small fields and rapidly decaying exceptional path events.

These are proposed uses; no subsequent application is recorded for this instrument.
